newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rain may reduce Australia cotton crop - trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rain may reduce Australia cotton crop - trade.

text.p: Heavy rain in northern New South Wales and southern Queensland appeared likely to reduce Australia's 1996/97 cotton crop, manager grower services of Namoi Cotton Co-operative, David Lindsay, said on Friday.
Still-current forecasts of a crop of 2.5 million 500-pound bales were looking highly unlikely, with the harvest more likely to emerge at 2.4 million bales, he told Reuters.
Heavy rain in the upper Namoi River area in New South Wales had waterlogged some crops, he said.
The lower Namoi was mostly flood protected and damage there was expected to be minimal, he said.
But it was a late season already for the 1996/97 Australian cotton, which was effecting yields, he said.
Current overcast weather was of concern and could delay picking further, he said.
Early picking of Australia's northernmost cotton crop, at Emerald in southeast Queensland, is due to begin in four to eight weeks.
Reports from other areas of the cotton region suggest that rain has not affected yields.
Heavy rain has fallen over coastal areas of Queensland and northern New South Wales throughout the past week from tropical cyclone Gillian, which dissipated toward the end of the week.
